definition: In computational neuroscience, SUPS (for Synaptic Updates Per Second) or formerly CUPS (Connections Updates Per Second) is a measure of a neuronal network performance, useful in fields of neuroscience, cognitive science, artificial intelligence, and computer science..
details: In computational neuroscience, SUPS (for Synaptic Updates Per Second) or formerly CUPS (Connections Updates Per Second) is a measure of a neuronal network performance, useful in fields of neuroscience, cognitive science, artificial intelligence, and computer science.

explainer.lead: SUPS measures neuronal network performance as synaptic updates per second, a unit for comparing how fast such networks compute. It matters in computational neuroscience and AI as a common performance yardstick.

tiers.eli5: It's a speedometer for a brain-like network, counting how many connections it updates each second.
tiers.practitioner: Researchers use it to report and compare the throughput of neuronal network simulations across neuroscience, cognitive science, AI, and computer science. A pitfall is that raw update counts say nothing about whether the simulation is biologically meaningful.
tiers.paperLevel: SUPS, formerly CUPS (Connections Updates Per Second), counts synaptic updates per second as a performance measure for neuronal networks. It is a throughput metric only.

explainer.example: Reporting a spiking network simulation's speed in SUPS so it can be compared against another network's update rate.
